ruleLines.allMustAnswer: All {{n}} must answer. Losing any one locks you out.
ruleLines.bothMustAnswer: Both must answer. Losing either locks you out.
ruleLines.singleMethod: If you lose your key, this one method is the only way back into the account.
ruleLines.secondMethodOffer: Add a second passkey from another device, or a hardware key if you have no second device.
ruleLines.platformFate: Two passkeys behind one platform account share its fate.
ruleLines.anyNOfM: Any {{n}} of these {{m}} recover this account. Losing more than {{spare}} locks you out.
ruleLines.eitherOneAlone: Either one alone can recover this account. Either one alone can also take it.
ruleLines.anyOneOfM: Any one of these {{m}} alone can recover this account. Any one alone can also take it.
ruleLines.togetherWithRequired: Together with your required methods, any {{n}} of these {{m}} recover this account. Losing more than {{spare}} locks you out.
ruleLines.togetherWithRequiredAndGroups: Together with your required methods and enough members of each other group to meet its threshold, any {{n}} of these {{m}} recover this account. Losing more than {{spare}} locks you out.
ruleLines.oneFailureDomain: One failure domain. These members fail together if their kind does.
ruleLines.differentPlaces: Keep the methods of your path in different places.
ruleLines.sizingRule: A group of any one of two is the shape this wallet prefers at two methods.
ruleLines.togetherWithGroups: Together with enough members of each other group to meet its threshold, any {{n}} of these {{m}} recover this account. Losing more than {{spare}} locks you out.
ruleLines.togetherWithRequiredEveryMember: Together with your required methods, every member of this group must answer.
ruleLines.togetherWithGroupsEveryMember: Together with enough members of each other group to meet its threshold, every member of this group must answer.
ruleLines.togetherWithRequiredAndGroupsEveryMember: Together with your required methods and enough members of each other group to meet its threshold, every member of this group must answer.

writes.submittingBody: Your key is sending one transaction. Do not close the wallet.
writes.notSent: The transaction was rejected before it reached the chain. Nothing changed.
writes.reverted: The transaction reached the chain and reverted. {{cause}} The gas it spent is gone.
writes.cancelReverted: Your cancel reached the chain and reverted. The attempt was already gone, executed or ended in the same block, and the gas it spent is gone.

gas.fundTitle: Fund the key that sends the recovery
gas.sendingKey: The key that sends this recovery
gas.sendingKeyPays: This key sends the recovery and pays its gas. The account cannot pay for itself until it is recovered.
gas.submissionAmount: Send at most {{amount}} to this key for the submission. The exact amount follows the network fee when you submit.
gas.secondFunding: Executing after the waiting period is a second transaction. This wallet asks you to fund this key again at execution due, at that day's fee.
gas.network: Send on {{network}}, the network of the account you are recovering.
gas.continuesOnItsOwn: This screen continues on its own once the funds arrive.
gas.alreadyFunded: Already funded? This step skips itself.
gas.continueUnlocks: Continue unlocks when the funds arrive.
gas.notEnoughGasAccountKey: Not enough gas on your account's key
gas.notEnoughGasSendingKey: Not enough gas on the sending key
gas.shortfall: Your account's key holds too little to send this. It needs {{amount}} more.
gas.shortfallSave: Your account's key holds too little to send this save. It needs {{amount}} more.
gas.shortfallSubmit: Your key holds too little to send this. Fund it, then submit again.
gas.shortfallCancel: Your account's key holds too little to send this cancel. Fund it, then cancel again.
gas.transferRouteNote: One transaction from your smart account to its own key.
gas.outsideRoute: Or send {{amount}} to this key from outside this wallet.
gas.transferIsAnOperation: A transfer out of the account the key operates is itself an operation that key must send and pay for. A key at zero therefore cannot take the first route alone.
gas.accountHoldsFunds: Your account holds the funds and its key sends the transactions.
gas.executionAmount: Send at most {{amount}} to this key for the execution. The exact amount follows the fee of that day.
gas.shortfallExecute: Not enough gas on the sending key. Fund it, then execute.
gas.networkOwner: Send on {{network}}, the network of this account.
gas.outsideRouteAlone: Send {{amount}} to this key from outside this wallet.
gas.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the address by hand.

writes.revertedSave: The transaction reached the chain and reverted. {{cause}} Nothing was saved, your recovery path is not active yet, and the gas it spent is gone. Everything you enrolled is still here.
writes.revertedSubmit: The transaction reached the chain and reverted. {{cause}} No waiting period has started and the gas it spent is gone. Everything you collected is still here.
writes.revertedExecute: Could not execute. The transaction reached the chain and reverted. {{cause}} The recovery is still ready and the gas it spent is gone.
writes.revertedEdit: The transaction reached the chain and reverted. {{cause}} Nothing changed, the gas it spent is gone, and your edits are still here.

causes.InvalidCommitment: The setup sent is one the recovery registry cannot accept.
causes.WrongSetupNonce: The setup number is not the one this transaction was built for.
causes.MethodStopped: A method in the path is under a security stop.
causes.MethodVetoedSpend: A method the recovery used is under a security stop. Nothing executes while the stop is on.
causes.MethodNotUsed: The named method was not part of this recovery.
causes.AttemptIgnoresPause: This recovery's setup does not honor a security stop.
causes.MethodNotStopped: The named method is not stopped.
causes.PlaceOutOfRange: An approval named a row the recovery path does not have.
causes.NoSetup: This account has no recovery setup under this recovery module.
causes.NoActiveAttempt: No recovery is running for this account.
causes.AttemptAlreadyActive: A recovery is already running for this account.
causes.WrongAttemptId: The attempt number is not the one the registry expects.
causes.SetupCommitmentMismatch: The recovery path sent does not match the setup on chain.
causes.StaleAttempt: The setup changed after this recovery was judged.
causes.CredentialMismatch: A method in the request does not match the one enrolled at that row.
causes.PlacesNotStrictlyIncreasing: The approvals are not in the order the registry requires.
causes.RequestExpired: The request arrived after its own deadline.
causes.ProofRejected: A method did not accept the approval given for it.
causes.RuleUnsatisfied: The approvals collected do not satisfy the recovery path.
causes.WaitNotOver: The waiting period has not ended yet.
causes.WrongPayload: The handover sent is not the one this recovery approved.
causes.BatchNotApproved: The transaction is not the one this recovery approved.
causes.MalformedHandover: The recovery module could not read the handover: it does not decode, names a zero key, or names one key on both sides.
causes.ReservedAuthority: The key being removed no longer holds control, or the new key already holds a privilege on this account.
causes.NotConsumable: This recovery cannot execute in its current state.
causes.unnamed: The chain gave no cause the wallet can name.

cancelGoneRoad.cancelByOwner: Your own key already cancelled it.
cancelGoneRoad.cancelByProofs: A set of approvals signed for cancel already ended it.
cancelGoneRoad.cancelByVeto: A security stop already ended it.
cancelGoneRoad.setupWrite: A change to the setup already ended it.

writes.revertedExecuteGone: Could not execute. The transaction reached the chain and reverted. {{cause}} The gas it spent is gone.
writes.gasCheckFailed: Could not finish the gas check. The node did not answer.
writes.replaced: Another transaction from this key took this one's place before it ran. Nothing changed.

ceremony.refusedNote: Refused · the device refused the request
ceremony.unreachableNote: Unreachable · the phone never connected · Try again
ceremony.notSupportedNote: Not supported · this document cannot be checked by this method

ceremony.testFailedNoMatch: The check did not match the method's key on chain.
ceremony.testUnavailableLine: The check could not run. The verifier could not be reached.
ceremony.notSupportedLine: This document cannot be checked by this method. The answer will not change.
ceremony.passkeyOrigin: This passkey works only from Kohaku on Chrome.
ceremony.providerRefused: Your passkey provider refused Kohaku. Create the passkey in your browser's own passkey store instead.
ceremony.relyingPartyMismatch: This passkey was created under a different Kohaku origin. It cannot answer from this one.
ceremony.syncedLoss: It follows the Apple or Google account that syncs it, so it survives losing this device. Whoever holds that account can start a recovery. If that account closes or you cannot reach it, this method is gone.
ceremony.deviceBoundLoss: It lives only on this device. Losing the device also removes this method, and the path with it where nothing else can recover.
ceremony.scanCode: Scan this code with the phone. The step runs there and this tab waits.
ceremony.keepTabOpen: Keep this tab open. The result arrives when you return to it.
ceremony.phoneReads: The phone that opens this reads the account and the new key. Do not forward the link.
ceremony.tabOnly: This step continues in a new tab.
ceremony.nothingToRun: There is no step to run here. Go back to the row that sent you.

ceremony.undeliveredNote: Not delivered · the result did not reach the row · Try again

ceremony.passportTunnel: Passport: your phone reads the chip in your passport. zkPassport runs the flow that carries this between the two devices.

records.expiredBody: The deadline passed on {{deadline}}. Every approval dies together.
records.voidTitle: Another recovery attempt was opened on this account
records.voidBody: Every approval you collected named an attempt number that attempt used up.
records.setupChangedBody: Every approval you collected was given under the old setup.
records.wipedNote: Nothing was submitted and nothing left the account. Every approval was wiped from this device. Only this reason is kept.
records.draftAge: Your setup is unfinished. Draft from {{date}}. Nothing is saved on chain until you confirm.
records.startOverNote: Start over discards the draft. Your created passkey is not deleted.
records.writeFailed: This device could not save your draft. Nothing changed. Try again.
records.loadFailed: This device could not read your draft.

disclosures.guardianPublication: A recovery publishes the whole recovery path on chain in the clear, every method in it and not only the ones it used. If a recovery uses this guardian, their address goes on chain in the clear. Even unused, anyone who can guess it can find it. Ask them first.
disclosures.smartAccount: If this address is a smart account, whoever controls it can approve for it.
disclosures.identity: This method shows the details on the document, not that you are the one using it now.
disclosures.passportPublication: If a recovery ever uses this method, the identifier your passport produces goes on chain in the clear, beside your account. Any later setup with the same passport can be linked to it.

costLines.save: Saving is one transaction your account's key pays.
costLines.saveDeploys: Saving is one transaction your account's key pays. It also deploys your account, so it costs more gas.
costLines.recovery: A recovery is sent and paid for by the recoverer's own key. It costs the account nothing.
costLines.cancel: Cancelling a recovery is one transaction your account's key sends and pays for. That key needs gas it holds outside the account.

socialRecovery.honestyNote: Recovery helps if you lose your key. It cannot stop someone who already has it.

presets.lead: One recovery path per account. Pick the shape that fits you. You can change it later in Settings.
presets.pickOne: Pick one · this becomes your recovery path

deviceAndGuardians.name: Your device and your guardians

editor.noGroup: No group yet. A group is any N of its members.
editor.duplicate: This method is already in your path. This wallet allows each method once.

rules.header: This wallet's rules while you edit
rules.requiredAnswers: A required method must always answer.
rules.enoughMembers: A group needs at least as many members as its threshold.
rules.thresholdAtLeastOne: A group's threshold must be at least one.
rules.thresholdCeiling: A group's threshold cannot be above 255.
rules.memberCeiling: A group cannot hold more than 255 members.
rules.oneRowPerMethod: One enrolled method sits in one row.
rules.atLeastOneMethod: A path needs at least one method.
rules.smallEnough: A path must be small enough to check in one block.
rules.zeroThresholdOwnRule: On a path with a required method or a second group, only this wallet refuses a threshold of zero.

picker.title: Add to your path
picker.lead: Pick something you already enrolled, or enroll something new.

editor.continueUnlock: Continue unlocks when your path has at least one method.

refusals.emptyGroup: This wallet cannot save a group with no members. Add a member or remove the group.
refusals.emptyGroupSlot: This wallet cannot save a group with a member that is not enrolled yet. Enroll it or remove it.
refusals.thresholdAboveMembers: This wallet cannot save a group that requires more members than it holds. Lower the threshold or add members.
refusals.thresholdBelowOne: This wallet cannot save a group whose threshold is below one. Require at least one member.
refusals.thresholdBelowOneOwnRule: This wallet cannot save a group whose threshold is below one. On a path with a required method or a second group, this rule is this wallet's alone.
refusals.thresholdAboveField: This wallet cannot save a threshold above 255. That is the most the kit's field can count.
refusals.memberCeiling: This wallet cannot save a group of more than 255 members. This limit is this wallet's own.
refusals.noMethod: This wallet cannot save a path with no method. Add at least one.
refusals.waitFieldWidth: This wallet cannot save a waiting period past the width the kit's field holds.
refusals.waitCeiling: This wallet cannot save a waiting period past the longest this picker offers.
refusals.tooLarge: This wallet cannot check a path this large in one block. Remove members or groups.
refusals.emptyRequired: This wallet cannot save a required method that is not enrolled yet. Enroll it or remove the row.
refusals.backupTooWide: This wallet cannot save a path whose hidden details are too large for the setup's backup. Remove members or groups.
refusals.actionUnsupported: This release cannot recover this account yet, so this wallet cannot save a setup for it.
refusals.thresholdWholeNumber: This wallet cannot save a threshold that is not a whole number. Type how many members must answer.

passkey.title: Set up your passkey
passkey.authenticators: Face ID, a fingerprint or a security key
passkey.explainer: A passkey is a key held by this device or your password manager. You approve a recovery with Face ID, a fingerprint or a security key. There is nothing to remember and nothing to write down.
passkey.createLine: Your device creates the key. It asks you for Face ID, a fingerprint or a security key, and nothing is sent to the network.
passkey.createOnPhoneInstead: Create it on your phone instead
passkey.testOffered: The access test is offered right after. Save works with or without the test.
passkey.testLead: Sign one test challenge with this passkey. The test runs locally.
passkey.testPassed: Your passkey signed a test challenge on this device. The test runs locally.

guardian.title: Add your guardians
guardian.lead: A guardian approves your recovery by signing with their own wallet.
guardian.pasteHint: Paste the address, or type a name such as bluejay.eth.
guardian.callBack: Before this guardian approves, they must call you back on a number they already hold. A guardian who can do that completes the check on the day.
guardian.ownerAnswer: The only other honest answer is I am the owner, which holds for a key you keep yourself and for nobody else.
guardian.checksumFailed: This address fails its checksum. Check it character by character.
guardian.nameResolves: {{name}} resolves to this address. A resolved name is what the address's owner chose, never a check.
guardian.nameUnresolved: This name does not resolve to any address.
guardian.noCode: No contract code at this address today.
guardian.smartAccountDetected: This address is a smart account.
guardian.notSameSeed: Not derived from this wallet's recovery phrase.
guardian.sameSeed: This address comes from the same seed as your key, so losing the seed loses both.
guardian.advisory: These checks are advisory. None of them stops you from saving.
guardian.howMany: How many must approve is set on the path, not here.
guardian.testedLine: This key signed the test challenge.
guardian.waitingForSignScreen: Waiting for the wallet's sign screen…

waitingPeriod.lead: A recovery never finishes at once. While the waiting period runs, the account's own key can cancel a recovery it did not start.
waitingPeriod.onePerPath: One waiting period covers the whole recovery path.
waitingPeriod.minimumDefault: This wallet needs a waiting period of 24 hours or more. The default is 48 hours.
waitingPeriod.belowMinimum: This wallet needs 24 hours or more.
waitingPeriod.pastCeiling: This wallet cannot save a waiting period this long. The longest it accepts is {{hours}} hours.
waitingPeriod.wholeHours: This wallet counts the waiting period in whole hours.
waitingPeriod.noticeWindow: The waiting period is your whole notice window. Open the wallet during the wait to see the banner for a recovery you did not start.
waitingPeriod.nothingElseWatches: Until you install Kohaku on another device, nothing else watches this account.
waitingPeriod.howToChoose: How do I choose a length?

level.title: Privacy level and recovery password
level.lead: This changes what a stranger can read about your setup, never who can recover the account.

private.label: Private
private.line: A stranger sees that this account has a recovery setup and nothing of what it is until a recovery runs, which publishes the whole rule on chain in the clear.

shapeVisible.label: Shape visible
shapeVisible.line: The shape of your setup is readable: {{shape}}. Which ones stays hidden.

public.label: Public
public.line: Everything is readable by anyone. No password is set and the card carries only the address.

exposure.guardians: Every guardian of your path is hidden from a stranger who cannot guess their address.
exposure.unguessable: {{items}} cannot be guessed at all and lose nothing before a recovery.
exposure.unguessableOne: {{items}} cannot be guessed at all and loses nothing before a recovery.
exposure.publication: A recovery publishes the rule with its waiting period and every method in it, so every method of your path is exposed, the ones it used and the ones it did not.

level.requiredAtPrivate: Required at Private and Shape visible.
level.tradeCard: Anyone holding the Recovery Card can read the recovery path and still cannot recover.
level.tradeLoss: Lose both the card and the password and a fresh device cannot begin a recovery.
level.unlockLine: Hidden values unlock with this recovery password during a recovery.
level.publicLine: No password is set. A fresh device rebuilds the setup from the chain alone, and the card carries only the address.
level.mismatch: The two recovery passwords you typed do not match.

review.title: Review and confirm
review.lead: This is what gets saved. Check it once, then confirm.
review.hostileMinority: With three or more members, choose a threshold a hostile minority cannot reach: a set that satisfies the rule can also cancel a recovery at once.
review.spareKey: A spare key on this account is the cheaper way to survive a lost key, and no help against a stolen one.
review.minimum: This wallet's minimum is 24 hours. The chain enforces none.
review.costsHeader: What a recovery costs and shows

publication.lead: A recovery publishes the whole recovery path on chain in the clear, every method in it and not only the ones it used.
publication.methodsAndGuardian: {{items}} becomes public and permanent, and so does this guardian's address if a recovery uses it. Even unused, anyone who can guess that address can find it.
publication.methodsAndGuardian_plural: {{items}} become public and permanent, and so does this guardian's address if a recovery uses it. Even unused, anyone who can guess that address can find it.
publication.methodsAndGuardians: {{items}} becomes public and permanent, and so do your guardians' addresses if a recovery uses them. Even unused, anyone who can guess those addresses can find them.
publication.methodsAndGuardians_plural: {{items}} become public and permanent, and so do your guardians' addresses if a recovery uses them. Even unused, anyone who can guess those addresses can find them.
publication.guardian: Your guardian's address becomes public and permanently tied to this account. Even unused, anyone who can guess it can find it.
publication.guardians: Your guardians' addresses become public and permanently tied to this account. Even unused, anyone who can guess them can find them.

trust.adminLine: This party can change the key this method trusts, so it could approve for this method.
trust.oneAcceptanceAway: {{address}} is one acceptance away from that role.
trust.recoverAlone: At a threshold of one, this party could recover the account alone.
trust.recoverAloneAny: This party could recover the account alone.
trust.passportRenewal: Renewing the passport ends this method.
trust.moduleAuthority: Once authorized, this module can act with the account's authority at any time.
trust.auditedOnly: This wallet offers the kit's audited recovery modules and nothing else.
trust.thirdPartyDeclaredRow: Third-party method · Not audited · the method's admin {{party}}
trust.thirdPartyLine: This method publishes no declaration of who it trusts.
trust.perAccountTrust: The trust a module carries is per account, not per module. Authorizing a second module trusts it with the whole account.
trust.nodeLightClient: Your node · a light client with its prover. It sees the request before the chain does.
trust.nodePlain: Your node · a plain node. It sees the request before the chain does.
trust.selfAttested: Every declaration above is the contract's own statement about itself.
trust.deadProvider: A method whose provider stops working is dead for good.

stop.party: {{party}} can stop this method and lift the stop.
stop.bothRoles: {{party}} holds both roles on this method: it can change the key this method trusts and it can stop this method. The same party decides both, so this stop is no answer to the risk the admin row names.
stop.noPause: The recovery registry and the recovery module carry no pause and no owner. The only stop in the kit is the one an identity method carries.
stop.ignoresStops: This release ignores every stop: a stop on a method will not stop your recoveries, and it will not stop a forged one against you either.

doors.none: Other doors on this account · None this wallet can see. The wallet cannot see every door, and the account is only as safe as its weakest one.
doors.unreadable: Other doors on this account · This wallet could not read them. The wallet cannot see every door, and the account is only as safe as its weakest one.
doors.keysBeside: {{count}} key beside the one a recovery removes
doors.keysBeside_plural: {{count}} keys beside the one a recovery removes
doors.marker: The code entry is the entry point's marker, which this account installed itself rather than a door anyone chose.
doors.validator: Any code entry that is not the marker is a validator somebody bound to this account.
doors.untouched: A recovery leaves them untouched. The account is only as safe as its weakest door.

otherDoors.cannotSeeEveryDoor: The wallet cannot see every door, and the account is only as safe as its weakest one.

card.title: Your Recovery Card
card.lead: Save it, print it or send it to another device. Keep it somewhere ordinary, a drawer, a folder or a safe, away from the device that holds your wallet.

lines.guide: To start recovery on any device, install Kohaku and choose Recover an account.
lines.cannotMoveFunds: This card alone cannot move funds.
lines.keepAway: Keep this card away from the device that holds your wallet.
lines.photograph: A photograph of this card plus the chain can read your recovery path. It still cannot recover.

card.reDownload: A new download asks your extension password.
card.whyNotOnCard: Why isn't my setup on the card?

card.wrongPassword: That is not your extension password. Try again.
card.passwordGone: Your recovery password is not on this device any more. Set it again on the privacy step to reveal it and carry the card.
